items.title: The Strange Situation has cultural biases
items.claim: Van IJzendoorn and Kroonenberg's 1988 meta-analysis of Strange Situation studies across 8 countries found what pattern?

options.text: Identical proportions of attachment types in all cultures

Higher rates of insecure-avoidant in Germany and insecure-resistant in Japan and Israel — but interpretation is contested: are these real attachment differences or measurement artefacts of an American-developed procedure?
The Strange Situation cannot be administered outside the US
No cultural variation exists in any developmental measure

items.reveal:
Takahashi (1990) noted Japanese infants are rarely left alone, so the Strange Situation may induce extreme distress that registers as 'resistant'. German samples (Grossmann) showed avoidance interpreted differently — culturally valued early independence.

IJzendoorn's later work (1999, 2008) emphasised within-culture variation often exceeds between-culture. The procedure's validity outside Western middle-class contexts remains debated.
items.why: Standardised procedures developed in one culture may measure different things in another. Cross-cultural psychology often needs methodological adaptation, not just translation.

items.title: The bystander effect story
items.claim: Darley and Latane (1968) showed that people are less likely to help when others are present. The often-repeated 'Kitty Genovese 38 witnesses' story has been challenged. What did later journalism find?
items.prompt: Which is closest to the current historical record?

options.text: There were probably far fewer witnesses than reported, and some did call police
There were no witnesses at all

items.reveal:
Manning, Levine and Collins (2007) and later reporting by the New York Times showed the original 1964 article overstated the number of witnesses and inattention.

The bystander effect as a laboratory phenomenon is robust, but the case used to illustrate it was inaccurate.
items.why: Findings can be real while their iconic illustrations are not. Textbooks now distinguish the experimental effect from the journalistic story.

items.title: Chronic stress activates the HPA axis
items.claim: The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis produces cortisol in response to stress. What does chronic activation cause?

options.text: Sustained elevation of cortisol is associated with immune suppression, abdominal fat deposition, hippocampal atrophy, and increased cardiovascular risk — moving stress from a psychological to a physiological problem
Cortisol stops being produced under chronic stress

items.reveal:
Hans Selye described the General Adaptation Syndrome (alarm, resistance, exhaustion) in 1936. Bruce McEwen's concept of 'allostatic load' (1998) extends this: the wear-and-tear of repeated stress responses contributes to chronic disease.

Whitehall studies (Marmot, 1967 onwards) linked low job control with worse health outcomes via stress pathways. The relationship between psychosocial stress and cardiovascular disease is robust across cohorts but causality is hard to isolate from confounders.
items.why: The mind-body distinction breaks down when looking at chronic stress. Psychological experience produces measurable biological change with health consequences.
